input.encoding: [N, M, source, piece_count, (u,v,w)*M, then piece records [left_child,right_child,leaf_arc_mask,boundary_count,boundary_order...]]
input.simple_planar_underlying_edge_bound: The number of distinct unordered endpoint pairs is at most 1 for N=2 and 3N-6 otherwise; each pair has at most one arc in each direction.
input.arc_model: Each record is one directed arc. Opposite arcs are optional and have independent signed weights.
input.embedding: Each piece supplies its boundary vertices in cyclic embedding order. The underlying graph is a connected planar embedding, all piece boundaries are cofacial in their listed order, and the induced directed distance blocks satisfy the Monge inequalities required by the profile.
input.hierarchy: Pieces are listed postorder. A leaf has left_child=right_child=-1 and a nonempty arc bitmask. An internal piece has two earlier child indices and leaf_arc_mask=-1. Leaf masks partition all M directed arcs. Each parent is the union of its children, children overlap on a nonempty separator, each child has at most ceil(2*parent_vertex_count/3) vertices, and every piece is connected.
input.boundary_definition: A piece boundary is the set of its vertices incident to an arc outside the piece, plus the source when the source belongs to the piece. The listed order is a permutation of exactly this set. The root boundary is the source alone.
input.negative_cycle_policy: Inputs must have no negative directed cycle. The bounded implementation checks the complete original directed graph before constructing DDGs and returns -1 if a negative cycle exists.

algorithm_profile.ddg: A piece DDG stores exact shortest-path distances between its ordered boundary vertices, using only arcs in the piece; unreachable pairs have infinite distance.
algorithm_profile.negative_edges: At each internal piece, one all-zero-source Bellman-Ford pass over the union of its two child DDGs finds feasible Johnson potentials. Every finite directed DDG arc is reweighted by w+h[u]-h[v].
algorithm_profile.monge_blocks: For each child boundary cycle, recursively split each interval into consecutive halves and add both directed cross-half matrices. Each ordered non-diagonal pair occurs in exactly one block. Before use, every block is checked against the Monge inequality.
algorithm_profile.online_dijkstra: Each directed block maintains activated left rows, the best (label+edge_distance, target_id, row_id) for each unsettled right column, and its settled-column set. Dijkstra repeatedly chooses the global minimum among tentative seed labels and block candidates, settles the target across blocks, and activates its outgoing rows.
algorithm_profile.bounded_data_structure: Boundary sizes are capped at 12. ActivateLeft, FindNextMinNode, and AddCurrentMinNodeToS preserve the FR online state machine but use bounded direct scans; the paper's amortized interval-tree/heap implementation is not included.
algorithm_profile.distance_expansion: Starting from the root source label, run the same reweighted block-Dijkstra once per internal piece to propagate exact labels to child boundaries. At a leaf, relax its at-most-three directed arcs to produce distances for all its vertices.
algorithm_profile.output: N signed 64-bit shortest distances in vertex-ID order, encoded as little-endian bytes without a count prefix. Unreachable vertices use INT64_MAX. Return the number of bytes written.
